Task: Expose all documented service and trading operations through Make targets
Description: Expose every operator operation as a thin Make target and document operations.

Before editing, inspect: the existing Makefile; mike_trade/cli.py, especially CANONICAL_COMMANDS, the global options --account/--scenario/--format/--confirm-live and the exit codes, plus the controls handlers from task s.3; mike_trade/controls/history_commands.py from task s.5; the dependency lock tooling and virtualenv conventions established earlier (for example the lock file and sync command); the systemd unit files and service helpers; the dashboard launcher; and existing docs. Make recipes must only invoke the CLI (and the dependency lock tool for install/update). They contain no business logic.

Rewrite or extend the Makefile:
(1) Variables: PYTHON ?= the project venv python, and CLI := $(PYTHON) -m mike_trade.cli. Pass-through operator variables are ACCOUNT, SCENARIO, SYMBOL, STRATEGY, KEY, VALUE, SINCE, UNTIL, LIMIT, FORMAT, OUT, RUN_ID and CONFIRM_LIVE. They are passed only as CLI flags or as the CONFIRM_LIVE environment variable.
(2) .PHONY declarations and a '## description' comment on every target. help (the default goal) prints all targets with their descriptions.
(3) Targets:
- install, update, doctor, config-show;
- providers, provider-check, broker-check, data-check;
- strategies, strategy-info, strategy-check, strategy-enable, strategy-disable, strategy-set;
- symbols, symbols-add, symbols-remove, symbols-enable, symbols-disable;
- start, stop, restart, status;
- dashboard, dashboard-start, dashboard-stop, dashboard-health, health;
- shadow-start, shadow-stop, shadow-list, shadow-create, shadow-reset;
- paper-start, paper-stop, paper-status;
- live-preflight, live-enable, live-start, live-disable;
- pause, resume, pause-symbol, resume-symbol, entries-disable, entries-enable;
- close, close-all, flatten;
- trail-status, trail-history, trail-policy-show, trail-policy-set, trail-reconcile;
- entry-limits, entry-limits-reset, cooldown-status;
- stop-status, stops-audit;
- positions, orders, balance, budget, reconcile;
- signals, evaluations, events, logs;
- report, report-daily, report-symbol, report-strategy, report-pairs, report-shadow, report-comparison, report-export;
- backtest, backtest-status, backtest-report, backtest-list;
- cache-status, cache-refresh;
- db-check, db-backup, db-restore-dry-run;
- test, test-unit, test-integration, test-paper, lint, typecheck;
- service-install, service-uninstall, service-status.
(4) Each non-tooling target invokes '$(CLI) <same-named canonical subcommand>' with pass-through flags. test/test-unit/test-integration are bounded by explicit test paths/markers. test-paper is credential-gated: it is skipped by the test suite when paper credentials are absent, and it never uses live credentials. lint and typecheck invoke the configured linters only.
(5) Live confirmation is enforced by the CLI. Make only forwards CONFIRM_LIVE and never sets it to YES by default.

Write docs/OPERATIONS.md, an operator runbook that documents every target with its variables and examples. It must explain:
- stop vs. flatten vs. close-all;
- pause vs. entries-disable, including that protection and reconciliation continue while paused;
- the live confirmation rule and the risk-reducing commands that are exempt;
- that order commands refuse while the engine is offline and nothing is queued;
- startup reconciliation and entry blocking;
- that UNMANAGED external positions are handled;
- the fee policy: broker-imported fees, labeled estimates, no hand-loaded fee files;
- report/export formats and reconciliation identity conventions;
- health and OFFLINE semantics;
- service install/uninstall on Ubuntu systemd;
- backup and restore dry run;
- test tiers, with the statement that ordinary tests never use live credentials.

Write tests/unit/test_make_targets.py. It parses the Makefile text and, when make is available, runs 'make -n <target>' with dummy variables (dry run only; never executes recipes). It asserts:
- every required target exists, is .PHONY, has a ## description and appears in the help output;
- each non-tooling recipe invokes '-m mike_trade.cli' with a subcommand present in mike_trade.cli.CANONICAL_COMMANDS;
- recipes contain no business-logic markers ('python -c', 'sqlite3', 'curl', 'alpaca', inline SQL, shell arithmetic on prices);
- no recipe sets CONFIRM_LIVE=YES;
- stop and flatten map to distinct subcommands;
- every target is documented in docs/OPERATIONS.md.
Phase: S
Acceptance criteria:
  - The Makefile defines every target listed in this task as .PHONY, with a ## description, and help is the default goal and lists all of them
  - Every non-tooling target recipe invokes $(PYTHON) -m mike_trade.cli with the same-named subcommand, and each such subcommand exists in mike_trade.cli.CANONICAL_COMMANDS
  - No recipe contains python -c, sqlite3, curl, provider SDK calls, inline SQL or other business logic; install/update invoke only the established dependency lock tool plus CLI doctor
  - No Makefile line sets CONFIRM_LIVE=YES; CONFIRM_LIVE is only forwarded from the operator environment
  - stop and flatten invoke different CLI subcommands, and the stop documentation states that protective stops and positions are left in place
  - test-paper is credential-gated and never references live credentials; test, test-unit and test-integration are bounded to explicit paths or markers
  - docs/OPERATIONS.md documents every Make target and covers stop/flatten/close-all, pause vs. entries-disable, live confirmation and exemptions, offline refusal without queuing, fee policy, report/export, health/OFFLINE, systemd service management, backup/restore dry run and test tiers
  - tests/unit/test_make_targets.py passes and uses only Makefile parsing and make -n dry runs, never executing recipes

# AGENTS.md

## Purpose

This repository is operated by an autonomous multi-agent system (abracapocus_2).
All agents must follow these rules when modifying the codebase.

---

## Core Principles

- Minimal blast radius: only modify what is required for the task
- Deterministic verification: all changes must be verifiable via code (tests, compile, scripts)
- No architecture drift: do not introduce new frameworks or major design changes unless explicitly required
- No unrelated refactors
- All changes must be reproducible from a clean clone

---

## Project Structure

- docs/ → design, plans, architecture constraints
- plans/ → master plans
- phases/ → phase definitions
- tasks/ → executable task documents
- backends/ → CLI backend adapters
- agents/ → specialist agents
- runtime/ → orchestration, routing, state
- reports/ → execution reports (DO NOT MODIFY MANUALLY)
- state/runtime_state.json → runtime state (DO NOT COMMIT)

---

## Task Execution Rules

- Always operate from a task document when available
- Respect:
  - selected_backend
  - verification_profile
  - acceptance_criteria
- If a task conflicts with architecture constraints or phase scope:
  - STOP and report conflict

---

## Backend Rules

- Backends must:
  - execute commands deterministically
  - capture stdout, stderr, exit_code
  - not silently fail
- Do not invent backend interfaces; use existing adapters
- Codex CLI, Aider, Gemini, Claude Code should be invoked through backends only

---

## Verification Rules

- Verification must be deterministic
- Preferred checks:
  - pytest
  - python -m py_compile
- Do not rely on model self-evaluation

---

## Execution Control Flow (PERMANENT ARCHITECTURAL RULE)

**HEURISTIC INFERENCE MUST NEVER PARTICIPATE IN ABRACAPOCUS EXECUTION CONTROL FLOW.**

Abracapocus must not determine execution success, failure, acceptance,
rejection, blocking, retry eligibility, phase progression, or completion from
heuristic inference. A heuristic is any conclusion that is *inferred* rather
than *directly established by an explicit executable contract or a concrete
runtime fact*.

Runtime status is derived ONLY from concrete, mechanically observable facts:

1. The backend process exit code. A backend that exits `0` (with no hard
   write-policy violation) is a successful execution.
2. Objectively observed hard write-policy violations (changed paths outside the
   declared allowed write paths).
3. Explicit operator-authored commands (task/phase verification the plan
   explicitly contains). Their raw results are reported, kept DISTINCT from
   backend execution status.
4. Objective orchestrator failures with direct evidence (backend could not
   launch, required document could not be parsed, subprocess infrastructure
   failed).

**Verification results are observational and must not rewrite backend execution
status.** A verifier returning non-zero must NEVER, by itself, turn a
successful backend execution into unverified, stop a phase, or trigger an
automatic rerun. Verification is the result of a command, not authority to
rewrite history.

**Execution control:** Task-local problems (non-zero exit, timeout,
write-policy violation, frame failure, backend launch failure) produce
acceptance status ``"unverified"`` with truthful evidence preserved. They
MUST NOT stop sibling tasks, later phases, or the plan. Only operator
cancellation (SIGINT/SIGTERM/dashboard cancel) may terminate a run
(acceptance status ``"interrupted"``). Dependencies are ordering constraints,
not acceptance gates — any terminal attempt outcome satisfies a dependency
edge. The status ``"failed"`` is banned from acceptance output.

Do NOT reintroduce -- under any name, feature flag, "advisory" wrapper, or
compatibility mode -- context completeness/sufficiency scoring, change or
architecture assessment used as a gate, intent/scope matching, reconciliation
gates, no-progress judgments, confidence/risk scores, model/LLM/reviewer
judgments over status, shadow/adaptive/secondary-verification gates, or
heuristic retry/failure-classification control flow. Failure classification may
only *summarize* an already-established concrete failure; it must never create
one. Retries are permitted only for explicitly defined mechanical backend
failures. Future agents must not add these systems back.

---

## Git Rules

- Do not commit:
  - runtime_state.json
  - reports/
  - logs/
  - virtual environments
- Do not modify .gitignore unless required by task
- Do not create excessive commits; prefer grouped logical commits

---

## Allowed Changes

- Implement task requirements
- Fix failing verification
- Update relevant tests
- Improve documentation tied to the task

---

## Forbidden Changes

- Changing architecture without explicit instruction
- Adding dependencies without justification
- Modifying unrelated files
- Deleting important files
- Bypassing verification

---

## Planning Rules

- Plans are multi-phase
- Completed sections are immutable
- Remaining sections may be updated
- Tasks must align with:
  - project brief
  - architecture constraints
  - active phase

---

## Reporting

- All executions must produce structured reports
- Reports must include:
  - changed files
  - verification results
  - assessment

---

## Behavior

- Do not ask unnecessary questions
- Do not stall execution
- Do not perform broad scans unless required
- Prefer direct action over analysis

---

## Priority Order

This ordering guides *implementation decisions* only. It does NOT make
verification an acceptance authority: verification results are observational
(see "Execution Control Flow"), and never override a concrete backend
execution result.

1. Architecture constraints
2. Task definition
3. Verification results (observational signal, not acceptance authority)
4. Plan guidance

If conflicts occur, follow this order.
